success_patterns: Most clues were answered by taking the entity that recurs across many search-snippet passages next to the clue's distinctive phrase (Tom Clancy, Appaloosa, Pituitary, Charley horse, Roman Empire). The agent trusted the repeated phrase and did not overthink.

Where the answer is a multi-word standard name or term, the agent kept the head noun. 'Roman Empire' and 'pituitary gland' were answered in full even though the clue said 'this empire' / 'this gland'. 'Charley horse' was answered for 'this term'. The bare modifier alone ('Roman', 'pituitary') would not have named the entity.
For epithet or attribution clues ('has called him "King of the Techno-Thriller"'), the agent answered with the full person name that the passages place next to the quoted phrase.
A quiz-thread line that reposted the clue followed by a guess ('Alex, is that INVENTION?') was treated as the answer line and copied. This was correct.
Titles were given bare, in standard capitalisation, without quotation marks ('Mary Had a Little Lamb'). This is already covered in Rule 4.

patch.reasoning: Two of eight successes ('Roman Empire', 'pituitary gland') kept the type noun the clue supplied ('this empire', 'this gland'). Rule 4 currently says never to append the role word, which could push a future agent to answer 'Roman' or 'pituitary'. A narrow exception is needed: keep the head noun when the bare modifier does not name the entity on its own. The exception must not undo the rule against 'Yalta Conference' or 'Sirius Satellite Radio', where the bare name stands alone. The other two edits record two behaviours that worked and were only partly covered: epithet-attribution clues, and thread lines that repeat the clue and then give a guess.

edits.target: do not append that role word to the answer.
edits.content: - Exception: keep the head noun when it is part of the entity's standard name and the bare modifier is only an adjective that does not name the entity by itself. 'Empire' clue -> 'Roman Empire' (not 'Roman'); 'this gland' -> 'pituitary gland' (not 'pituitary'); 'this term for a leg cramp' -> 'Charley horse' (not 'Charley'). Test: would a trivia answer key accept the bare word alone? If yes ('Sirius', 'Roanoke', 'Amazon', 'Yalta'), drop the type word. If the bare word is just a modifier, keep the full standard name as the passages spell it.

edits.target: Choose the entity that recurs across many passages together with the clue's other named entities (e.g. the title in 'Thunder Road (film)' pages). Do not talk yourself out of a well-supported entity.
edits.content: - Epithet or attribution clues ('The New York Times Magazine has called him "King of the Techno-Thriller"', 'Critics dubbed her ...') ask for the PERSON. Find the passages that repeat the quoted epithet beside a name and answer with that full name as the passages write it ('Tom Clancy'). Ignore the publication or critic named in the clue.

edits.target: Archive lines may also be formatted 'CATEGORY | clue text | answer'.
edits.content: A forum or quiz-thread line that reposts the clue and then offers the answer, even as a question to the host ('Alex, is that INVENTION?'), counts as an archive hit. Take that word.
